setting: A fictional one-to-one catch-up between a team lead and a team member about a late piece of work.

presentation.situation: You own {{task}}, due {{due}}. It is late because {{cause}}. {{name}}, your team lead, asks what happened. Explain it without blaming anyone, say what it affects, and propose a specific next step.
presentation.opening: Thanks for making time. {{task_cap}} was due {{due}}, and {{stakeholder}} has asked me about it. What happened, and what happens next?

brief.you_are: You are the team member who owns {{task}}.
brief.situation: It was due {{due}}. It is late because {{cause}}. It affects {{impact}}. You could finish it by {{new_date}} if {{condition}}.
brief.task: Explain what happened without blaming anyone, say what the delay affects, and propose a specific next step with a date.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} understands the cause and the impact, and you have agreed what happens next and by when.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: Owns the late piece of work
goals: Give a clear, honest update and a next step

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: Your team lead, who has to answer to {{stakeholder}}

card.want: A straight account, and a date to give {{stakeholder}} today.
card.hidden_need: Was surprised by this delay, and wants earlier warning next time.
card.attitude: Calm, direct and a little under pressure. Not looking for someone to blame.
card.speech: Plain workplace English. Short questions. Uses the details the other person gives.
tactics: Ask 'so what does that affect?' if no impact is mentioned
Ask 'by when, exactly?' about any vague date
Ask who else is involved if someone gets blamed

pressure.gentle: Patient, and helps with one easy question.
pressure.challenging: Asks why nobody raised this earlier, firmly and without insults.

ledger.text: The work is {{task}}, which was due {{due}}.
{{name}} has to give {{stakeholder}} a date today.

objectives.evidence: The learner says what happened factually, and owns their part rather than blaming a person.
alternatives: The supplier file arrived late and I didn't flag it soon enough

objectives.evidence: The learner says what the delay affects, for whom.
alternatives: This means the client report goes out two days later

objectives.evidence: The learner proposes a concrete action with a date or owner. A vague promise does not count.
alternatives: I'll finish by Thursday noon and send you a draft on Wednesday

examples: I'll ... by ..., and I'd like your help with ...
prerequisites: Read the cause, the impact and your options in the briefing.

beats.goal: Hear what actually happened, without blame.
signals: \b(?:what happened|because|the reason|arrived|i didn'?t|i should have|ran into|took longer|waiting|delayed by)\b
opportunity: Walk me through it. What actually got in the way?
I'm not looking to blame anyone. I just need to understand what happened.
beats.orient: I'm your team lead, and the work you own is late. Tell me what got in the way. Your brief has the reason.
fallback: What actually got in the way?
Can you tell me what happened?

opportunity: Okay. So what does that affect?
What's the knock-on effect if it stays late?
beats.orient: Now tell me what this delay affects. Who or what depends on this work?
fallback: Who else does this hold up?

beats.goal: Leave with a specific next step and a date to report.
signals: \b(?:i will|i'?ll|by (?:today|tomorrow|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|noon|next|the end)|next step|i propose|i suggest|can you help|could you help)\b
opportunity: What's the plan, then? I need a date for {{stakeholder}}.
By when, exactly? And do you need anything from me?
beats.orient: Last part. Tell me what you'll do next and by when. Your brief says what date is possible, and what you would need.
fallback: What's the plan, and by when?

closing_line: Okay, that's clear. I can tell {{stakeholder}} that. Thanks for being straight with me.

o1.good: Facts first, in a sentence or two, owning your part and not naming a culprit.
common_mistakes: A long story with no point
o1.micro_lesson: Describe what happened, not who is at fault. Then say what you could have done sooner.
o1.model: The supplier file arrived late, and I didn't flag the risk early enough.
o1.smaller_step: Say in one sentence what got in the way.

o2.good: Saying what the delay changes for other people, so your lead can act.
common_mistakes: Saying only that it is late
o2.micro_lesson: Your lead must answer to others. Tell them what this changes for those people.
o2.model: This means the client report goes out two days later.
o2.smaller_step: Name one person or thing the delay affects.

o3.good: One concrete action with a date, and a clear request if you need help.
common_mistakes: 'I'll try to get it done soon'
Waiting to be told what to do
o3.micro_lesson: Bring a plan, not only a problem. Give a date your lead can repeat to others.
o3.model: I'll finish by Thursday noon. Could you get me that sign-off by Wednesday?
o3.smaller_step: Say the day you can finish it.

variants.name: Nadia
variants.cause: the data export arrived three days late and you did not flag the risk
variants.impact: the sales team's Friday customer review
variants.condition: you get the corrected export by Wednesday
variants.help: chasing the data team for the corrected export

variants.name: David
variants.cause: testing found more problems than the plan allowed for, and two remain
variants.condition: someone else takes your support shift on Tuesday
variants.help: covering the support shift on Tuesday

variants.name: Ayesha

variants.condition: the supplier resends the file this morning
